plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and showy rose-like flowers. It is widely cultivated in temperate gardens and thrives in partial shade with acidic, well-drained soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant used to make tea, and its seeds yield camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that blooms on bare branches in the cold of winter, producing fragrant five-petaled flowers. It is a beloved symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to southern China; cultivated in Japan, Korea, and Taiwan
plants.funFact: Because it flowers amid snow and frost, the plum blossom is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' in Chinese art, along with pine and bamboo.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub with large, spectacular flower heads made up of colorful bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It is adapted to nutrient-poor soils and fire-prone fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (peak from December to February, with blooms in other seasons too)
plants.location: South Africa, in the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape
plants.funFact: The King Protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its genus is named after the Greek god Proteus because of the wide variety of forms it takes.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with fern-like leaves that becomes covered in brilliant clusters of flowers in the warm season. It is a favorite shade and ornamental tree in tropical and subtropical regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); also blooms in dry seasons in some tropical regions
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in Australia, Brazil, and tropical regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Although it is a spectacular and common street tree around the globe, the Royal Poinciana is endangered in its native habitat in Madagascar.
